chunks: And Aban narrated from Isma'il who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who rented land from another man and said: 'Rent it to me for such-and-such amount, whether I cultivate it or not, I will pay you that amount.' However, the man did not cultivate the land. He (the Imam) said: 'The owner has the right to take it with his money; if he wishes, he may waive it, and if he wishes, he may not waive it.'

key_terms.بِمَالِهِ: with his money / from his wealth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fixed rent for land if the tenant does not cultivate it?
ai.summary: Recorded by Aban ibn Taghlib in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, this hadith clarifies the validity of fixed-rent leases (ijarah) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the tenant's failure to cultivate does not invalidate the contract. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) grants the landlord full discretion to enforce the payment or waive it, reflecting the principle of contractual freedom in agricultural tenancy. This ruling underscores the importance of clear stipulation of terms in Islamic commercial law, distinguishing between fixed rent and sharecropping models.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3894 - Aban narrated from Isma'il who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about a man who rented land from another man and said: "Rent it to me for such-and-such amount, whether I cultivate it or not, I will pay you that amount." However, the man did not cultivate the land.
Imam (as) said: "The owner has the right to claim the payment. If he wishes, he may waive it, and if he wishes, he may not waive it."
